_comment_20260821: Cloned from .20260820.0N (see AGENTS.md's 20260820 entry for that round's A/B1/B2/C changes, all retained here unchanged). Two new changes this round, both from a detailed post-hoc analysis of the completed .20260820.0{0-7} studies (see AGENTS.md's 20260821 entry for the full writeup): (1) pca_pc1_dominance_key: "pca_explained_variance_ratio" -> "pca_size_normalized_standardized_explained_variance_ratio", with max_pca_pc1_ratio_factor 1.3 -> 2.0 -- the hard degenerate-PC1-dominance guard was checking the *raw* PCA family's PC1, but the .20260820 objective no longer weights that family at all (fully replaced by pca_size_normalized_standardized_*, that round's fix C) -- guard and objective were measuring two different things. Recomputing full weighted compute_stats_distance for every one of the 201 PC1-dominance-pruned trials across the 8 .20260820 studies (using their already-archived candidate_stats.json, exactly as run_trial would have scored them had the guard not fired) showed that in 2/8 studies the single best trial among the pruned pool would have beaten that study's true best surviving trial, and that the guard was disproportionately walling off high lib_size_scale (81% pruned above 1.3, vs 12% pruned in [0.6, 1.3]) -- exactly the region that most helps close the gene_var_mean/gene_var_std shortfall (lib_size_scale is the #1 rank-regression driver of both, partial coef +0.59/+0.66). Retargeting the guard at the size-normalized-standardized family's own PC1 (the metric the objective actually scores) and re-picking the factor (empirically, ratio-to-target bins of 0.7-1.6 in that family cover .20260820's best-trial range and average distance ~0.03-0.05, while >2.0 already shows mean distance >0.20 -- a real degenerate region) keeps the guard aligned with what's actually being optimized, at a threshold chosen from the same real data rather than carried over from the old family's calibration. (2) search_space.lib_size_mean upper bound 6.0 -> 8.0 -- pooled across all 751 .20260820 completed trials, gene_var_mean/gene_var_std ratio-to-target rise monotonically with lib_size_mean all the way to the search space's upper bound (no plateau: trials with lib_size_mean>5.7 still average only ~0.61x target on gene_var_mean), and all 8 studies' best trials cluster near that boundary (lib_size_mean 4.96-5.95, mean 5.25) -- the bound itself, not the objective, was the limiting factor.

weights._comment_excluded_keys: Explicitly excluded (weight 0.0) rather than merely omitted below: an omitted key still defaults to weight 1.0 in compute_stats_distance, not 0.0 -- these 12 keys were previously omitted by oversight and ended up silently contributing ~25% of the total objective across the 20260811.* studies (see AGENTS.md's Known Issues and compute_stats_distance's own docstring). gene_mean_mean/gene_mean_std/gene_var_mean/gene_var_std were re-added above at weight 1.0 (this config) after the .20260812.* studies showed those four consistently undershooting the target by 2-4x while contributing nothing to the objective; the remaining percentile duplicates (gene_mean_p5/p25/p50/p75/p95, gene_var_p5/p25/p50/p75/p95) and mean_var_log_slope/mean_var_log_corr stay excluded to avoid overweighting the same underlying distribution shape multiple times. Set any of these to a nonzero value if you want to score them too.
